bodyEn: The document known as “the oldest football season ticket in the world” promises its bearer access to every Burnley home game of the 1884-85 season. It is a ticket that predates the Football League by four years, with all the fixtures played against east Lancashire neighbours. All the same, the legend on the ticket carries a stern warning: “This card is not transferable. Any member violating this rule will be at once expelled from the club.”

For Burnley 1884 read Manchester United 2026. While the oldest remaining season ticket is safely preserved at Turf Moor, at Old Trafford 685 season tickets were voided this summer after a club investigation found evidence of their having been resold on the secondary market. United said such practices “undermine fair access to tickets for genuine supporters and have no place at Manchester United”. United fan groups again protested against the actions of the club’s ownership, claiming: “The way you treat us is a disgrace.”

Nearly 150 years after fans started paying up front to watch their team, the season ticket remains a key component in the success of English football. It is also an enduring source of conflict between supporters and clubs, with tensions seemingly reaching new heights. Arsenal, like United, have continued to act against the perceived misuse of tickets, suspending nearly 74,000 club accounts since they began a crackdown in 2024. This summer Chelsea became the latest club to insist on minimum levels of attendance to retain your ticket for the following season. Bournemouth moved 600 season-ticket holders to accommodate new hospitality seats and 14 out of the 20 top-flight sides raised their season-ticket prices.

Season-ticket holders have long felt undervalued. But there is a growing sense, especially among fans of the biggest clubs, that they are falling ever further down the pecking order as economic imperatives change. It is a feeling that intensified after a World Cup that seemed precision-tooled to extract as much money as possible from the most devoted fans. One Liverpool supporter crystallised common fears when he appeared on The Overlap at the start of the season arguing that a big club would soon try to get rid of season tickets altogether. The clip went viral.

The Football Supporters’ Association argues that clubs’ present behaviour shows an antagonism towards season-ticket holders. “There’s a sense from supporter groups at the most successful teams that their club executives and owners don’t fully appreciate season ticket holders and would rather have stadiums full of one-off visitors,” an FSA spokesperson said.

“Those who only measure things by the bottom line see season-ticket holders as a group whose matchday spend is lower than the once-a-year fan who will fill their bag at the club shop and pay a bigger premium for their ticket. It’s a shortsighted vision.”

The claim that clubs want to swap longstanding supporters for one-off tourists is at the heart of many fans’ fears over season tickets and, to a certain extent, it bears out. Dominik Schreyer, a professor of sports economics at the WHU Otto Beisheim School of Management in Düsseldorf, says season tickets “come at a cost” for clubs.

“In the Premier League, demand is way higher than seat supply,” Schreyer says. “But season ticket holders get discounted seats, right? They are also more likely to be no-shows. When they do come they spend less on food, less on merchandise and they come later to the stadium. They also don’t churn, because these tickets are so scarce that nobody in their right mind would give them away. Every year the average age grows by one because there is no one new getting tickets. So for the clubs, there are a lot of economic problems from their season-ticket holders.”

That, however, is only one side of the ledger. “What we should not forget is that, in the end, season-ticket holders are part of a product that, in the case of the Premier League, is marketed to a global audience,” Schreyer says. “They are creating an atmosphere. Season ticket holders are also used to all the rules and the rituals and the songs, the moments that make this experience very special. So tourists want to come because they want to experience it. If you were to get rid of all the season-ticket holders, you would have all the operational and coordination costs of doing it and the product would not be the same any more.”

There are other reasons why season tickets work for clubs, not least because they generate a largely predictable amount of revenue that turns up at the same time each year (at the very end of the season where it can be usefully deployed to help with transfer spending limits). For most clubs, it would not be feasible to replace season-ticket holders with one-off fans even if they wanted to. But with the average number of season tickets at any given Premier League fixture running at 75% of all tickets, is there a case that this number should not be set in stone? Could access to matches be broadened without killing off a part of what made them great?

“In theory, you could give all the seats to season-ticket holders and still have a lot of tickets for new fans if you manage it effectively,” Schreyer says. “You just need to change the mechanism in order to get the ticket that is unused on to the secondary market.”

This is what is happening at a number of clubs, with fans being asked to return their tickets for resale if they are not being used. But these requests have often come with warnings that tickets could be removed should fans not comply. Some of the tension around season tickets is simply because clubs are not talking clearly or frequently enough with fans. “Clubs don’t communicate that well,” Schreyer says. “I don’t understand why they don’t get fans on board better. You can make things so transparent.”

It is instructive looking across the Premier League at the season-ticket policies of each club, the way they were announced and the response they received from supporters. Brentford raised prices for the first time in five years, but faced minimal pushback. Brighton’s 3% rise was backed by the fan advisory board. Chelsea and Tottenham froze prices but still found themselves at odds with their fanbase.

The season ticket is a device as old as the game itself but has grown to become a symbol of the connection between fanbases and clubs. Disputes over the importance of season tickets may prove to be a harbinger of their demise, but may equally be better understood as a sign of the dysfunction at the top of our biggest clubs.

items.titleZh: 赛季票持有者对在俱乐部地位下降感到担忧
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳等英超俱乐部严打违规转让赛季票，引发球迷对自身地位的担忧。
bodyZh: 被称为“世界现存最古老足球季票”的文件承诺其持有者可以观看伯恩利1884-85赛季的所有主场比赛。这是一张比英格兰足球联赛早四年诞生的球票，所有比赛都是对阵兰开夏郡东部的邻居。尽管如此，票根上的传奇字样还是带有一个严厉的警告：“此卡不可转让。任何违反此规则的成员将被立即驱逐出俱乐部。”
对于1884年的伯恩利来说，这就如同2026年的曼联。虽然现存最古老的季票完好无损地保存在摩亚球场，但在老特拉福德，今年夏天有685张季票在俱乐部调查发现其被转售到二级市场的证据后被作废。曼联表示，这种做法“破坏了真正的支持者获得球票的公平途径，在曼联没有立足之地”。曼联球迷群体再次抗议俱乐部所有者的行为，声称：“你们对待我们的方式简直是一种耻辱。”

在球迷开始预付费用观看他们支持的球队近150年后，季票仍然是英格兰足球成功的一个关键组成部分。它也是支持者与俱乐部之间持久的冲突来源，紧张关系似乎达到了新的高度。与曼联一样，阿森纳继续采取行动打击被认为滥用球票的行为，自2024年开始打击行动以来，已暂停了近7.4万个俱乐部账户。今年夏天，切尔西成为最新一家坚持要求最低出勤率以便在下赛季保留球票的俱乐部。伯恩茅斯调整了600名季票持有者的座位以容纳新的贵宾席，在20支英超顶级联赛球队中，有14支提高了季票价格。

长期以来，季票持有者一直觉得自己被低估了。但人们越来越感觉到，特别是在最大俱乐部的球迷中，随着经济要求的变化，他们在俱乐部心目中的排序正在不断下降。在经历了一世界杯之后，这种感觉更加强烈，这届世界杯似乎是经过精确设计的，旨在从最忠实的球迷身上榨取尽可能多的金钱。一名利物浦支持者在赛季初出现在《The Overlap》节目中时，阐明了人们共同的担忧，他认为一家大俱乐部很快就会彻底取消季票。这段视频在网上广为流传。
足球球迷协会（Football Supporters’ Association）认为，俱乐部目前的行为表明了对季票持有者的敌意。FSA发言人表示：“来自最成功球队的球迷群体有一种感觉，他们的俱乐部高管和老板并没有充分重视季票持有者，而是更愿意让球场里坐满一次性游客。”
“那些只按底线衡量事物的人认为，季票持有者的比赛日消费低于一年只去一次的球迷，后者会在俱乐部商店里大肆采购，并为球票支付更高的溢价。这是一种短视的愿景。”
俱乐部希望用一次性游客取代长期支持者的说法是许多球迷对季票担忧的核心，在某种程度上，事实的确如此。杜塞尔多夫WHU奥托·拜斯海姆管理学院体育经济学教授多米尼克·施赖尔（Dominik Schreyer）表示，对于俱乐部来说，季票“是有代价的”。
施赖尔说：“在英超联赛中，需求远高于座位供应。但季票持有者的座位是有折扣的，对吧？他们也更有可能缺席。当他们来的时候，他们在食物上的花销更少，在周边商品上的花销也更少，而且他们到球场的时间也更晚。他们也不会流失，因为这些球票非常稀缺，任何头脑清醒的人都不会放弃它们。由于没有新人获得球票，平均年龄每年都在增长一岁。因此，对于俱乐部来说，他们的季票持有者带来了很多经济问题。”
然而，这只是账目的一面。“我们不应该忘记的是，归根结底，季票持有者是英超联赛所面向的全球受众产品的一部分，”施赖尔说。“他们正在营造一种氛围。季票持有者也习惯了所有的规则、仪式、歌曲以及让这种体验变得非常特殊的时刻。所以游客想要来，是因为他们想体验这一切。如果你要取消所有的季票持有者，你将承担所有的运营和协调成本，而且产品将不再是原来的样子。”

季票对俱乐部管用的原因还有其他，其中最主要的原因是它们产生了一笔基本可预测的收入，这笔收入每年在同一时间到账（在赛季结束时，可以有效地用于帮助应对转会支出限制）。对于大多数俱乐部来说，即使他们愿意，用一次性球迷取代季票持有者也是不可行的。但是，鉴于任何一场英超比赛中季票的平均数量占所有球票的75%，这个数字是否不应该一成不变？是否可以在不扼杀比赛伟大之处一部分的前提下拓宽观看比赛的渠道？
施赖尔说：“从理论上讲，如果你能有效地管理，你可以把所有的座位都给季票持有者，同时仍然为新球迷留出大量的球票。你只需要改变机制，把未使用的球票放到二级市场上。”
许多俱乐部正在发生这种情况，球迷如果不用球票，就会被要求将其退回以供转售。但这些要求往往伴随着警告，即如果球迷不遵守规定，球票可能会被取消。围绕季票的一些紧张局势，仅仅是因为俱乐部与球迷沟通不够清晰或不够频繁。“俱乐部的沟通做得不是很好，”施赖尔说。“我不明白为什么他们不能更好地让球迷参与进来。你可以把事情变得非常透明。”
纵观英超联赛中各俱乐部的季票政策、公布方式以及受到的球迷反应，是很有教益的。布伦特福德五年来首次提高价格，但面临的阻力微乎其微。布莱顿3%的涨幅得到了球迷咨询委员会的支持。切尔西和托特纳姆热刺冻结了价格，但仍然发现自己与球迷群体不和。
季票是一项与比赛本身一样古老的装置，但它已经成长为球迷群体与俱乐部之间联系的象征。关于季票重要性的争端可能被证明是它们消亡的先兆，但也同样可以被更好地理解为我们最大俱乐部高层功能失调的信号。

bodyEn: Mikel Arteta has agreed a long-term contract extension with Arsenal that includes a hefty pay rise in recognition of his success last season and could take his reign as the manager beyond a decade.

The three-year deal he signed in September 2024 expires at the end of this season and talks have been ongoing since May when Arsenal ended their long wait to be champions. Negotiations were put on hold during the summer transfer window but the Spaniard has reached a ­verbal agreement to extend his stay for a second time.

The length of the contract is unknown but it is understood Arteta, who took over from Unai Emery in December 2019, will commit his future for at least another three years. The 44-year-old is the Premier League’s longest-serving manager after the departure of Pep Guardiola from Manchester City at the end of last season.

Arsenal have been keen to reward Arteta for transforming the club. His current contract is believed to be worth about £10m a season plus a £5m bonus for reaching the Champions League. The new deal will cement his status as one of the best-paid managers in the world.

As well as leading Arsenal to a first Premier League title since 2004, Arteta last season guided them to the Champions League final, which they lost to Paris Saint-Germain in a penalty shootout in Budapest. The club started this season with seven straight wins in all competitions before Saturday’s surprise 3-0 defeat at Brighton.

Arteta reiterated before that game that he was relaxed about his contract situation. “I think we are all very much aligned,” he said. “Whenever the time is right, we’ll get that done. There is nothing to be concerned about. I think we both have the same ambition and the same will.”

items.titleZh: 米克尔·阿尔特塔同意续约，预计将执教阿森纳至2030年
items.summaryZh: 阿尔特塔与阿森纳就长期续约达成口头协议，新合同将包含大幅加薪。
bodyZh: 米克尔·阿尔特塔已同意与阿森纳签下一份长期的合同延长协议，其中包括大幅加薪，以表彰他在上赛季取得的成功，并可能使他的主教练任期超过十年。
他在2024年9月签署的三年生效合同将于本赛季结束时到期，自5月份阿森纳结束漫长等待夺得冠军以来，双方一直在进行会谈。谈判在夏季转会窗口期间曾被搁置，但这位西班牙人已经达成口头协议，第二次延长其执教时间。
合同的具体长度尚不清楚，但据了解，于2019年12月接替埃梅里的阿尔特塔将至少再承诺未来三年。在瓜迪奥拉上赛季末离开曼城后，这位44岁的教练成为了英超执教时间最长的现任主教练。
阿森纳一直希望奖励阿尔特塔对俱乐部的改造。据信他目前的合同价值约为每年1000万英镑，外加晋级欧冠的500万英镑奖金。新合同将巩固他作为世界最高薪主帅之一的地位。
除了带领阿森纳夺得自2004年以来的首个英超冠军外，阿尔特塔上赛季还率队杀入欧冠决赛，但在布达佩斯举行的点球大战中输给了巴黎圣日耳曼。在周六客场0比3意外负于布赖顿之前，俱乐部在本赛季各项赛事中取得了开局七连胜。
阿尔特塔在赛前重申，他对自己的合同状况感到轻松。“我认为我们所有人的目标高度一致，”他说，“只要时机成熟，我们就会搞定。没有什么好担心的。我认为我们双方有着相同的雄心和意志。”

bodyEn: In the week that 16-year-old Max Dowman has been thrust into the spotlight, it was another teenager who gave us a glimpse of the future in Brighton’s impressive win over Arsenal. Charalampos Kostoulas – nicknamed ‘Babis’ in his homeland, in homage to former Argentina striker Gabriel Batistuta – has already started twice as many Premier League games as he did in his first season in English football, when he was a backup for Danny Welbeck. The 19-year-old repaid Fabian Hürzeler’s faith in him against the reigning champions. Despite his tender years, Kostoulas already possesses the physical attributes to mix it with the best. He caused Gabriel Magalhães and company problems all afternoon, capping it off with a brilliant goal from 25 yards, his third in eight days. “We always knew that he’s capable of scoring goals out of nowhere,” said Hürzeler. “He just has this intrinsic motivation of really improving every day. He gets more and more professional, he understands the demands from the Premier League more, he understands our demands.” Ed Aarons
Match report: Brighton 3-0 Arsenal

Alexander Isak may have been Liverpool’s match-winner on Andoni Iraola’s return to Bournemouth, but it was an afternoon to celebrate defence rather than attack. Liverpool’s front four, signed for a combined £400m, were shorn of fluidity and chemistry. The real stars were in defence, with Ronald Araújo strong at right-back and Jérémy Jacquet commanding at centre-back. Liverpool have kept three straight clean sheets in the league for the first time since the start of 2024-25, and Jacquet’s partnership with Virgil van Dijk is blossoming. Last week the 21-year-old, a £60m arrival from Rennes, was named in Zinedine Zidane’s France squad in his first senior call-up. “He is adapting really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said of Jacquet. “I think in the first games, physically he was feeling the change of rhythm, he was finishing with cramps, really tired and we had to sub him. Today [Sunday] has been a step forward.” Ben Fisher
Match report: Bournemouth 0-1 Liverpool

Michael Carrick is far too phlegmatic to describe anything in such terms, but Manchester United’s game at Fulham was a must-win for the head coach – and they failed to win it. Going into the extended international break, United desperately needed a positive, but instead had to settle for a draw, clinched by Matheus Cunha. Despite the late equaliser, there were plenty of worrying signs for Carrick. One might have assumed United would come out all guns blazing at Craven Cottage in an attempt to seize control and change the narrative after a poor week, in which they had lost twice. Yet for long periods they were lethargic, lacking intensity off the ball and looking short of snap and fizz in the final third. Of particular concern to Carrick will be United’s profligacy in attack; they managed 29 shots at Fulham, but only six were on target and their goal needed a huge deflection to beat Bernd Leno. Dominic Booth
Match report: Fulham 1-1 Manchester United

With Dean Henderson absent from the Crystal Palace net and upcoming England squad, James Trafford had a further chance to impress Thomas Tuchel. Admittedly, Trafford spent a long time being very quiet and barely had anything to do in the first half, but after the break he showed why he is so highly thought of, costing Leeds more than £40m in the summer. The former Manchester City goalkeeper made a fine save down to his right from a Yéremy Pino free-kick when the Spaniard surprised him from the edge of the box. Furthermore, Trafford’s ability with the ball at his feet makes him a true competitor for Jordan Pickford at international level. If he carries on being a calming influence at Elland Road, he could become his country’s No 1 before too long. Will Unwin
Match report: Leeds 0-0 Crystal Palace

For an initial €20m (£17.2m) outlay to Ajax last summer, Brian Brobbey appears a bargain at No 9 as the 24-year-old’s hat-trick in Sunderland’s 5-3 loss at Manchester City underlined. These were the Dutchman’s first goals – all poacher’s finishes – in the sixth game of the season but Régis Le Bris had been unconcerned. “It’s really positive for a striker [to score three] – when you don’t score it’s still possible to tell the story differently [that he is failing] but for us it is really clear that he is a good striker and he’s getting better game after game. It’s just a question of time,” said the manager, who believes his striker is improving. Brobbey was left disappointed despite his hat-trick. “It’s hard being on the losing side when you’re scoring three goals,” he said. Jamie Jackson
Match report: Manchester City 5-3 Sunderland

All three promoted clubs have victories on the board following Coventry’s gutsy win at Nottingham Forest. By far the best team in last season’s Championship, Coventry’s struggles were in danger of souring their return to the top division. Jay Dasilva’s superb goal and an organised performance offered a remarkable turnaround from last Sunday’s hammering by Brighton. They now enter the bumper international break with optimism. As Frank Lampard noted, facing Arsenal, Manchester City and Brighton in three of their first four games has not been a kind reintroduction. Their defender, Stephen Mfuni, 18, delivered an assured Premier League debut. On loan from Manchester City, Mfuni received rave reviews in a four-month spell at Watford, another youthful defender to make a strong impression, alongside Jannik Schuster at Brentford and Luka Vuskovic at Brighton. Though was it Mfuni that Caleb Yirenkyi tripped over for the VAR decision that denied Forest an equaliser? Zapruder-esque footage from Forest fans suggests it might have been. John Brewin
Match report: Nottingham Forest 0-1 Coventry

By the end, the talk had switched to Brentford’s attacking potency, both from set plays and through the quiet probing of Mikkel Damsgaard, but this was a victory rooted in their defending. Jannik Schuster arrived from Salzburg in the summer for a fee of around £16m and is already beginning to look like a typically astute Brentford signing. The 20-year-old made his league debut as a substitute for the injured Nathan Collins against Sunderland, made his first start against Bournemouth and excelled against Chelsea, making 12 clearances, winning three aerial duels and blocking three shots. Perhaps more than anything else in football, defending is about structure but, still, it was striking to compare Schuster’s performance with that of the three Chelsea central defenders, who cost a combined £127m despite Levi Colwill being a youth product. Jonathan Wilson
Match report: Brentford 3-0 Chelsea

In attempting to get a handle on the latest Tottenham horror show, Saturday’s 3-2 home defeat by Aston Villa, Roberto De Zerbi bemoaned his side’s lack of resolve in tough moments. “Leaders have to be leaders”, he said. That Spurs lack leaders is clear but the void makes itself felt not just in weak defending. A dominant first half ended goalless for Spurs because of an absence of anyone grabbing the game by the scruff of the neck. The £50m signing Mohammed Kudus came on at half-time, but only made things worse. Only when James Maddison came on and Kudus went wide did Spurs regain shape and focus. De Zerbi appears to be taking a cautious approach to reintegrating Maddison, who missed a year of football with an ACL injury, but the Spurs No 10 has the ability and the self-confidence to impose himself on Premier League matches. De Zerbi might need to hasten his reintroduction. Paul MacInnes
Match report: Tottenham 2-3 Aston Villa

Following an ultimately hard fought 2-1 home win against Hull, Newcastle and their new manager, Matthias Jaissle, were left with a respectable eight points from the opening five Premier League games. But what have we learned along the way? Principal conclusions include: 1) Keeping the outstanding England left back, Lewis Hall this summer was imperative; 2) There will be times when Sean Steur requires resting, and moments when he makes mistakes, but the 18-year-old midfielder is an immensely exciting talent capable of shaping games; 3) A current tally of nine injured first-team players suggests Jaissle needs to modify his training regime; 4) Newcastle’s current lack of an orthodox centre forward and a natural No 10 makes Jaissle’s preferred 4-2-3-1 system hard to pull off; his squad are arguably better suited to playing three at the back; 5) Judging by Newcastle’s refusal to surrender to a spirited Hull, Jaissle is winning hearts and minds. Louise Taylor
Match report: Newcastle United 2-1 Hull City

Aside from the latest VAR nonsense, Stuart Attwell’s biggest call at Hill Dickinson Stadium was to show Abdul Fatawu a second yellow card for simulation. Despite Gary O’Neil’s claim to the contrary, the referee deserves all credit for doing so. The Ipswich winger was enjoying a productive afternoon and Everton were seething over the decision to disallow Thierno Barry’s header when Fatawu anticipated contact from James Garner and dived. He became only the third player in the last six Premier League seasons to receive a second yellow card for simulation. O’Neil admitted Fatawu had “moved his leg towards it a bit” and that he had spoken to the 22-year-old about not giving the referee a decision to make. But the Ipswich manager’s insistence there was “no desperate need for the referee to get involved” jarred. It was cheating, plain and simple, and the game would benefit from referees punishing it more frequently. It is also a disgrace that Fatawu was racially abused online afterwards. Ipswich and the relevant authorities are investigating the incident. Andy Hunter
Match report: Everton 1-0 Ipswich

items.titleZh: 英超周末战报：10大热点聚焦
items.summaryZh: 布莱顿击败阿森纳，年轻球员闪耀英超赛场。
bodyZh: 在16岁的小将马克斯·道曼成为焦点的一周里，又有一名青少年球员在布莱顿令人印象深刻地战胜阿森纳的比赛中让我们看到了未来。查拉姆波斯·科斯图拉斯——在祖国被称为“巴比斯”，以向阿根廷前锋加布里埃尔·巴蒂斯图塔致敬——本赛季在英超联赛中的首发场次已经是他在英格兰足球第一个赛季的两倍，当时他是丹尼·维尔贝克的替补。这位19岁的球员用对阵卫冕冠军时的表现回报了法比安·许尔泽的信任。尽管年纪尚轻，科斯图拉斯已经具备了与顶级球员对抗的身体素质。他整个下午都在给加布里埃尔·马加良斯等人制造麻烦，并在最后用一记25码外的精彩进球为比赛画上句号，这是他在八天内的第三个进球。
比赛报道：布莱顿 3-0 阿森纳

亚历山大·伊萨克可能是利物浦在安东尼·伊劳拉重返伯恩茅斯时的制胜功臣，但这是一个属于防守而非进攻的下午。利物浦价值总计4.04亿英镑的前场四人组缺乏流畅性和化学反应。真正的明星在后防线上，罗纳德·阿劳霍在右后卫位置上表现强劲，热雷米·雅凯在中后卫位置上威风凛凛。利物浦自2024-25赛季开始以来首次在联赛中连续三场保持零封，雅凯与维吉尔·范戴克的搭档也日渐成熟。上周，这位以6000万英镑从雷恩加盟的21岁球员首次入选了齐内丁·齐达内的法国国家队大名单。
比赛报道：伯恩茅斯 0-1 利物浦

迈克尔·卡里克为人处世十分冷静，绝不会用这种词汇来形容任何事情，但曼联客场对阵富勒姆的比赛对这位主教练来说是一场不容有失的比赛——而他们未能取胜。在漫长的国际比赛日到来之前，曼联迫切需要一场积极的比赛结果，但最终只能接受由马修斯·库尼亚锁定的平局。尽管有迟来的扳平比分，但对卡里克来说依然存在许多令人担忧的迹象。人们原本以为曼联会在克拉文农场全力以赴，试图在经历了一个输掉两场比赛的糟糕一周后掌控局面并扭转舆论。然而，在很长一段时间里，他们表现得死气沉沉，无球时缺乏强度，在进攻三区也显得缺乏活力和灵动。
比赛报道：富勒姆 1-1 曼联

由于迪恩·亨德森缺席水晶宫的大名单以及即将到来的英格兰国家队，詹姆斯·特拉福德获得了进一步打动托马斯·图赫尔的机会。诚然，特拉福德在很长一段时间里表现得非常低调，上半场几乎无事可做，但在中场休息后，他展现了自己为何在今夏让利兹联花费超过400万英镑的原因。这位前曼城门将精彩地扑出了耶雷米·皮诺的任意球，当时这位西班牙球员在禁区边缘突施冷箭。此外，特拉福德脚下控球的能力使他成为国家队中乔丹·皮克福德的真正竞争者。如果他能继续在埃兰路球场发挥稳定军心的作用，他可能会在不久的将来成为国家队的一门。
比赛报道：利兹联 0-0 水晶宫
去年夏天以初始2000万欧元（1720万英镑）的价格从阿贾克斯引进布赖恩·布罗贝，现在看来这笔9号位的签约非常划算，正如这位24岁球员在桑德兰3-5负于曼城一战中上演帽子戏法所证明的那样。这是这位荷兰人在本赛季第六场比赛中打入的处子球，全部都是门前抢点破门，但雷吉斯·勒布里斯对此并不担心。
比赛报道：曼城 5-3 桑德兰

随着考文垂在诺丁汉森林取得勇敢的胜利，所有三支升班马都已在积分榜上取得了胜利。作为上赛季英冠联赛中表现最好的球队，考文垂一度面临状态挣扎，这险些让他们的顶级联赛回归之旅蒙上阴影。杰伊·达席尔瓦的精彩进球和有条不紊的战术执行，与上周日被布莱顿惨痛击败形成了惊人的逆转。他们现在带着乐观的心情进入密集的国际比赛日。正如弗兰克·兰帕德所指出的那样，前四场比赛中有三场要面对阿森纳、曼城和布莱顿，这样的重返英超赛程并不算友好。他们的后卫、18岁的斯蒂芬·姆富尼交出了一份令人安心的英超首秀答卷。
比赛报道：诺丁汉森林 0-1 考文垂

到最后，讨论的焦点已经转向了布莱顿的进攻威力，无论是通过定位球还是米克尔·达姆斯高冷静的穿针引线，但这场胜利的根本还在于他们的防守。雅尼克·舒斯特在夏天以大约1600万英镑的身价从萨尔茨堡加盟，现在已经开始展现出一笔典型的精明布莱顿签约。这位20岁的球员在对阵桑德兰时替补受伤的内森·柯林斯完成了联赛首秀，在对阵伯恩茅斯的比赛中迎来了第一次首发，并在对阵切尔西时表现出色，完成了12次解围、赢得了3次空中对抗并封堵了3次射门。
比赛报道：布莱顿 3-0 切尔西

在试图理解托特纳姆热刺最新的一场灾难——周六主场2-3不敌阿斯顿维拉时，罗伯托·德泽尔比感叹球队在艰难时刻缺乏骨气。“领袖必须起到领袖的作用，”他说。热刺缺乏领袖是显而易见的，但这种真空不仅体现在薄弱的防守上。热刺在上半场占据统治地位却以0-0收场，正是因为缺少一个能够挺身而出掌控比赛的人。身价500万英镑的签约穆罕默德·库杜斯在半场替补登场，但却让情况变得更糟。直到詹姆斯·麦迪逊上场、库杜斯拉到边路后，热刺才重新找回了阵型和专注度。
比赛报道：热刺 2-3 阿斯顿维拉

在经历了一场艰难的2-1主场战胜赫尔城的比赛后，纽卡斯尔联及其新任主帅马蒂亚斯·雅伊斯勒在前五场英超联赛中拿到了可敬的八分。但一路上我们学到了什么？主要的结论包括：1）今年夏天留住杰出的英格兰左后卫刘易斯·霍尔是势在必行的；2）有时需要让肖恩·斯特尔轮休，他也会犯错，但这位18岁的中场球员是一个极其激动人心且能够左右比赛的天才；3）目前一线队有9名受伤球员，这表明雅伊斯勒需要调整他的训练方案；4）纽卡斯尔目前缺乏正统中锋和天然10号位，这使得雅伊斯勒青睐的4-2-3-1体系很难施展；5）从纽卡斯尔拒绝向顽强的赫尔城屈服来看，雅伊斯勒正在赢得人心。
比赛报道：纽卡斯尔联 2-1 赫尔城

除了最新的VAR争议之外，斯图尔特·阿特维尔在希尔迪金森球场做出的最大判罚是因假摔向阿卜杜勒·法塔武出示第二张黄牌。尽管加里·奥尼尔提出了相反的说法，但这位裁判做出这样的判罚完全值得称赞。这位伊普斯维奇边锋当时正在享受一个高产的下午，埃弗顿对取消蒂尔诺·巴里的头球破门的决定感到愤怒，当时法塔武预判了来自詹姆斯·加纳的接触并顺势倒地。他成为了过去六个英超赛季中第三位因假摔吃到第二张黄牌的球员。奥尼尔承认法塔武“把腿往那个方向靠了一点”，并且他曾与这位22岁的球员谈过，要求他不要给裁判留下做决定的空间。
比赛报道：埃弗顿 1-0 伊普斯维奇

bodyEn: Mikel Arteta admitted Arsenal were taught a lesson by free-scoring Brighton as their 100% start to the season was abruptly ended on Saturday. Not since 10 May 2023 – 1,224 days ago – when the same opponents won 3-0 at the Emirates Stadium had the Premier League champions lost by three goals. But they were second-best throughout as Pascal Gross, Charalampos Kostoulas and Chema Andrés rounded off a comprehensive victory.

“They deserved to win the game and it’s a big lesson for us,” said a disappointed Arteta, who felt his players were not their usual combative selves. “From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear.
“We put ourselves in trouble one time, two times, three times and we need to get out of that much quicker than that. That’s one of the biggest lessons that we have to take from the game.

“We knew how tough it was going to be and the first thing we had discussed was about the first part. If you don’t get out of that first part as winners, it will be extremely difficult to dominate the game and to have any probability of winning the game. At this level, it’s extremely important to respect and to understand [that] before anything else.”

Asked whether this was a wake-up call after nine straight league wins that included them being crowned champions for the first time in 22 years in May, Arteta said: “For us it’s crystal clear. We knew and we talked for two days about what we have to do here. We played the fourth away game in a really short period of time.

“We know what it takes to win every single match and we know what it’s going to take to win against Leeds when we come back. That’s not a surprise, but it doesn’t take away the disappointment and emotional state we have”

Brighton have recorded victories over the reigning champions in the past three seasons and with 16 goals from five matches are all but certain to go into the international break as the division’s top scorers. Fabian Hürzeler compared the 35-year-old Gross to “a good wine” after he was instrumental in the win and praised his team’s collective efforts.

items.titleZh: 阿尔特塔：布赖顿配得上胜利，这对我们是深刻教训
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳本赛季全胜战绩终结，阿尔特塔承认球队遭遇惨痛失利。
bodyZh: 米克尔·阿尔特塔承认，随着周六本赛季的全胜战绩戛然而止，火力全开的布赖顿给阿森纳上了一课。自2023年5月10日（即1224天前）同样是对手在酋长球场以3比0取胜以来，这支英超冠军球队从未在单场比赛中净负三球。但随着帕斯卡尔·格罗斯、哈拉兰博斯·科斯图拉斯和切马·安德雷斯锁定了一场完胜，阿森纳在全场比赛中均处于劣势。
“他们配得上赢得这场比赛，这对我们来说是一个深刻的教训，”失望的阿尔特塔说道，他认为球员们没有展现出平日里的拼搏精神。“从第一个界外球开始你就能感觉到，这太明显了。”
“我们一次、两次、三次给自己制造了麻烦，我们需要更快地摆脱这种状况。这是我们必须从本场比赛中吸取的最大教训之一。”
“我们知道比赛会有多艰难，我们讨论的第一件事就是关于开局阶段。如果你不能在开局阶段占得先机，想要掌控比赛并有任何获胜的可能将极其困难。在这个级别，在其他任何事情之前，尊重并理解这一点极其重要。”

“我们知道赢得每一场比赛需要付出什么，我们也知道当我们回来对阵利兹联时需要付出什么。这并不意外，但这并没有消除我们的失望和情绪状态。”
布赖顿在过去三个赛季中都战胜了卫报的卫冕冠军，并且在5场比赛中攻入16球，基本确定将在国际比赛日到来时成为该联赛的头号射手。法比安·许策尔在格罗斯在这场胜利中发挥关键作用后，将其比作“陈年好酒”，并称赞了球队的集体努力。

“每个人今天都有这种心态：‘我需要先生存防守，我们作为一支球队防守，’”他说。“我们希望通过赢得微小的胜利来应对这场比赛。每个人都谈论进球是一场胜利，但微小的胜利可以是第一个界外球、第一个角球、赢得第一个头球、赢得第一次抢断。”
“如果你赢得了这些微小的步骤，如果你把它们单独庆祝为胜利，那么你就可以融入比赛。然后你可以获得越来越大的胜利。”

bodyEn: So much for the new Invincibles. Arsenal were brought back down to earth with a shuddering bump by a scintillating display from Brighton as Fabian Hürzeler’s vibrant side celebrated the club’s 125th anniversary in style.

The special edition shirts they wore to mark the occasion will end up being collector’s items after the Premier League champions were ripped apart. Arsenal were attempting to record an eighth successive victory in all competitions to start the new campaign for the first time since 1903 when they were still known as Woolwich Arsenal.

Instead, it is Brighton – inspired by first-half goals from the veteran stand-in captain, Pascal Gross, and the exciting teenager Charalampos Kostoulas – who find themselves in third place, two points behind Arsenal. New signing Chema Andrés made the points safe from a corner 12 minutes into the second half. That meant Arsenal conceded three goals for the first time since December 2023 in all competitions and Mikel Arteta will be most concerned that it could easily have been more against the division’s top scorers, 16 in five games.

The home supporters waved blue and white flags before kick-off as the players swapped their usual kits for a deep blue limited edition shirt that was inspired by their first season in Southern League Division Two in 1901. That has caused controversy among fans after originally being listed on sale for £150 in a package that included a letter of authenticity from the club owner, Tony Bloom, and a keyring. Given this is the only time they will wear it, those who shelled out will be pleased they did now.

What has made Brighton’s goalscoring exploits so impressive is that they have managed it almost completely without their first-choice attack due to injury, while last year’s top scorer, Danny Welbeck, was sold to Chelsea in the summer. Georginio Rutter returned as a late substitute, but the damage had already been inflicted by then thanks to Gross and Kostoulas.

Jurriën Timber looked leggy on his first start since March and Bruno Guimarães was disappointing on his first Premier League start for Arsenal. Myles Lewis-Skelly’s energy and drive in midfield was sorely missed in the week he was recalled to the England squad.

From the first whistle, Kostoulas – signed last summer for £30m – led Brighton’s fearsome press that provoked Arsenal into a number of uncharacteristic errors, including a misplaced pass from Guimarães that forced David Raya to tip a deflected effort from the 19-year-old around the post. Raya was also guilty of donating possession to the lively Yasin Ayari in a dangerous position. Arsenal and Arteta looked rattled for the first time this season.

Christos Tzolis could not take a rare opportunity on the break after being picked out by Bukayo Saka and they were made to pay for it just after the half-hour mark. Perhaps wary of the unmarked Ayari to their left, Gabriel Magalhães and Riccardo Calafiori were slow to challenge Gross when he received the ball on the edge of Arsenal’s area from Kostoulas and the veteran picked his spot perfectly off the inside of the post.

Ayari came close to doubling the lead five minutes before half-time when he fired into the side-netting before Kostoulas did. Saka had just spurned a great chance to equalise after being set up by Martin Ødegaard and once again Gabriel was guilty of ball watching as the Greek striker thumped the ball past Raya from 25 yards.

Arteta immediately sent out Max Dowman, who scored two goals against Ipswich in midweek, to warm up. He must have been tempted to throw the 16-year-old on at the start of the second half as Kostoulas went close again for Brighton.
It was too late once Andrés nodded in at the far post from a pinpoint Gross corner. “Are you Tottenham in disguise?” sang the delighted Brighton fans.

Arteta introduced Dowman with 10 minutes remaining as he emptied his bench. But having been knocked off the top of the Premier League on goal difference courtesy of this heavy loss, there will be plenty of soul-searching during the three-week international break for the Arsenal manager.

items.titleZh: 布莱顿3-0大胜卫冕冠军阿森纳
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳客场0-3不敌布莱顿，遭遇本赛季首场失利。
bodyZh: 所谓的新不败之师暂告一段落。在法比安·许策尔充满活力的球队以精彩的表现庆祝俱乐部成立125周年之际，阿森纳被无情地打回原形。
在英超卫冕冠军被彻底击溃之后，他们为纪念这一时刻而身穿的特别版球衣最终将成为收藏品。阿森纳原本试图自1903年（当时他们被称为伍尔维奇阿森纳）以来首次在新赛季各项赛事中取得开局八连胜。
然而，凭借老将代理队长帕斯卡尔·格罗斯和令人兴奋的19岁小将哈拉兰博斯·克斯图拉斯在上半场的进球，布莱顿升至积分榜第三位，落后阿森纳两分。新援切马·安德烈斯在下半场开始12分钟后通过角球锁定胜局。这意味着阿森纳自2023年12月以来首次在各项赛事中单场失球达到三球，而米克尔·阿尔特塔最担心的是，面对联赛中进球最多的球队（5场比赛打进16球），失球本可能更多。
主场球迷在开球前挥舞着蓝白相间的旗帜，球员们则换上了深蓝色限量版球衣，其灵感源自他们1901年在南部联赛乙级联赛的第一个赛季。此前该球衣定价150英镑并包含俱乐部老板托尼·布鲁姆的亲笔信和钥匙扣，这在球迷中引发了争议。鉴于这是他们唯一一次穿这件球衣，那些买单的人现在应该会感到高兴了。
布莱顿的进球表现之所以如此令人印象深刻，是因为他们在主力进攻球员几乎全部因伤缺阵的情况下做到了这一点，而上赛季的最佳射手丹尼·维尔贝克也在夏天被卖给了切尔西。热尔尼奥·吕特作为替补在最后时刻复出，但凭借格罗斯和克斯图拉斯的出色发挥，伤害在那之前就已经造成了。
尤里安·廷贝尔自3月以来的首次先发显得有些疲惫，布鲁诺·吉马良斯代表阿森纳的英超首秀也令人失望。在中场缺少了迈尔斯·刘易斯-斯凯利在本周重回英格兰代表队时的活力与冲击力。
从比赛的第一声哨响开始，去年夏天以3000万英镑引进的克斯图拉斯就带领布莱顿展开了凶猛的前场逼抢，迫使阿森纳犯下了多起不应该的失误，其中包括吉马良斯的一次失误传球，迫使大卫·雷亚扑出了这名19岁小将的折射射门。雷亚还在危险地带将球权送给了活跃的亚辛·阿亚里。阿森纳和阿尔特塔看起来在本赛季首次显得有些慌乱。

在newsletter推广之后
克里斯托斯·齐奥利斯未能抓住萨卡传球创造的难得反击机会，他们在半场刚过不久就为此付出了代价。加布里埃尔·马加良斯和里卡多·卡拉菲奥里或许是忌惮左侧无人盯防的阿亚里，在克斯图拉斯将球传到阿森纳禁区边缘时，他们反应迟缓未能及时贴防格罗斯，这位老将冷静推射击中立柱内侧破门。
在上半场结束前五分钟，阿亚里的一脚抽射击中边网，随后克斯图拉斯也险些破门。萨卡刚刚浪费了一次由马丁·厄德高创造的绝佳扳平机会，加布里埃尔再次因注意力不集中，目送这名希腊前锋在25码外将球轰入雷亚把守的大门。
阿尔特塔立即派出了在周中对阵伊普斯维奇时打进两球的马克斯·道曼去热身。当克斯图拉斯再次为布莱顿威胁球门时，他一定很想在下半场开始时就换上这位16岁的小将。
当安德烈斯接格罗斯精准的角球在远门柱头球破门时，一切都为时已晚。“你们是托特纳姆热刺假扮的吗？”高兴的布莱顿球迷高唱道。
阿尔特塔在比赛还剩10分钟时换上道曼，用完了所有换人名额。但由于这场惨败导致净胜球劣势从而跌出英超榜首，阿森纳主帅将利用为期三周的国际比赛日进行深刻的反思。

items.titleEn: Premier League news: Carrick brushes aside questions over future, Arteta salutes ‘extraordinary’ Dowman
items.summaryEn: United head coach believes it will take ‘a lot longer than one or two’ setbacks before he is concerned about his job Continue reading...
bodyEn: Michael Carrick said it would take more than one or two defeats before he came under internal pressure as the Manchester United head coach.

United lost 3-2 to Brighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, having led 2-0 at Old Trafford. That followed Sunday’s 1-0 home loss to 10-man Manchester City. United also went down 2-0 at Hull on the opening day of the season and conceded a late equaliser at Everton at the beginning of the month. The results have caused Carrick to come under scrutiny and he was reminded before Sunday’s visit to Fulham that his predecessors, Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, were sacked after 30 months and 14 months, respectively, in the job.

“It will be a lot longer than one or two games of results,” Carrick said when asked when he might come under pressure from United’s hierarchy. “It’s irrelevant for me. I know the club, I know the role, I know what’s expected here in terms of playing at a certain standard.

“In terms of the future and ownership and how long I’ve got, it’s totally nothing, it’s ridiculous to think that way in the position I’m in; it’s just not on the radar. It’s two or three games we haven’t had certain results. We’ve got to perform and we’ve got a lot of games to plan for.”

Carrick is content to take ownership of his team’s performance. “That’s why I’m here. It’s my responsibility, I’m fine with that,” he said. “It’s not a blame game. We always search for things to look at and find the blame, sometimes it gets too much. Blame me, it’s no problem, but it’s not about blaming people. It’s about finding solutions. It’s a collective thing. I know where we want to go and we want to get there fast. We don’t like losing matches, but it doesn’t affect what we do next.”
The 45-year-old was asked if he needs to show more emotion on the touchline. “I need to show more emotion? In what way?” he replied. “What do you want me to show?”

On Friday JJ Gabriel travelled to Barcelona for discussions regarding potentially joining the club, with United understood to have found out via the media despite the 15-year-old being registered with them.

On Tuesday Gabriel told United he wanted his registration rescinded because he wishes to join another club. Real Madrid have a firm interest and it is understood Gabriel and his advisers travelled for preliminary talks with Barcelona.
Carrick said: “The situation will work itself out, whatever way it’s going to work itself out. Making sure he’s OK is the important thing.” Jamie Jackson
Mikel Arteta has praised Max Dowman’s “extraordinary” transition from schoolboy to Arsenal first-team squad member and backed the teenager to make more of an impact this season.

Dowman became the first 16-year-old since Wayne Rooney in October 2002 to score twice for a Premier League club in Arsenal’s victory over Ipswich in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday, after bursting on to the scene last year. That was his first appearance of the campaign, having been an unused substitute on four occasions as Arsenal have won all seven of their fixtures. Dowman, who has been training with Arsenal’s first team since he was 14, completed his GCSEs in the summer and he will study for a BTec qualification after deciding against taking A-Levels. Arteta said Dowman’s development was still being carefully managed by Arsenal after a couple of years of having to balance his studies.

“It’s not easy,” said the Arsenal manager. “That’s what tells you about the craziness of the age and the environment he still lives in with the demands and the competition he needs to face during the week. But the way he has handled it, him and the family, it has been extraordinary. If he is here, he has to be here in all conditions and we cannot treat him differently in many aspects.”

Dowman is in contention to be on the bench to face Brighton on Saturday as Arsenal attempt to make it eight successive victories to start the season for the first time since their promotion season as Woolwich Arsenal in 1903-04. Arteta is convinced more opportunities will come his way sooner rather than later. “That’s the best way to knock on the door: to do it on the pitch, not in the office,” he said. “What Max did the other day, alongside all the players as well, that haven’t played that many minutes, it was really impressive.”

Premier League regulations do not allow players under 17 to be sent out on loan but Luton are understood to have registered an interest in Dowman, who was coached by their manager, Jack Wilshere, when he played for Arsenal’s under-18s. Arteta said it was possible Dowman could be allowed to leave in January, by which point he will be 17, but that his immediate future was at Arsenal.

“We haven’t really listened to any of the possibilities because we were crystal clear that we wanted to have him in the squad, that we wanted him to be part of the pre-season and then start to see where we are from there,” Arteta said.

“We will evaluate every six months, where we are and what is the best thing for him to do and then make the right decision. It depends on a lot of factors – what he needs and what the team needs as well, the availability we have in the squad, the minutes that he is playing and the qualities of those minutes. We have to be open but now the focus is to be here and to impact the team.” Ed Aarons

Roberto De Zerbi has insisted Sandro Tonali was not feeling the pressure of his price tag despite a mixed start to life at Tottenham. The midfielder became the most expensive player in the club’s history when he joined from Newcastle for £92.5m in the summer.

De Zerbi made a big play to sign Tonali amid interest from Manchester City and Arsenal, delivering a two-hour sales pitch to his fellow Italian to convince him to move to north London. He outlined how central Tonali would be to his plans and explained what he could expect from Spurs’ fans and the team’s style of football.

Tonali has started all four Premier League games this season – in which Spurs have drawn twice and lost twice without scoring – but has produced underwhelming defensive numbers and created only three chances.

De Zerbi revealed he had spoken to the 26-year-old about the weight of the price tag and claimed the player “doesn’t feel the pressure about that”. The Spurs manager pointed out that Tonali took time to adapt in his first season at Milan in 2020 before becoming one of the most sought-after young midfielders in the world once he settled there.

De Zerbi said “the adaptation has been not so fast” at Tottenham “but it can happen”, adding: “It is not so easy to change city, to change everything, for the players. Sometimes the adaptation is immediate, sometimes you need more time.”

Tottenham’s struggles in front of goal have not been helped by Tonali’s inability to create chances for the forwards. The goalless draw against Everton was the first in 140 games at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and followed a 0-0 at Nottingham Forest, thereby equalling Spurs’ tally of goalless games in the previous 181 matches. The last time they recorded three or more consecutive goalless draws in the league was 25 years ago under George Graham, when they went to four.

It is a remarkable run, especially after a summer spend of more than £300m, which leaves Spurs in 17th going into Saturday’s game against Aston Villa, who have also struggled after a summer of major change.

De Zerbi maintained he was happy with Tonali’s performances – even though he believed they could improve – and described him as “a complete midfielder”. “His physical characteristics are to play box-to-box but he started his career as a playmaker. He’s good enough with the ball, he’s good enough without the ball.” Sam Cunningham

Daniel Farke said Dominic Calvert-Lewin was “like a good wine” after the in-form striker’s call-up into Thomas Tuchel’s England squad. The 29-year-old has been included in the Three Lions’ squad for their Nations League matches after scoring four goals in six appearances in all competitions this season.

Calvert-Lewin was given a standing ovation by Leeds fans as he was withdrawn late on in Monday night’s 4-1 win against Newcastle at Elland Road. “Dominic is like a good wine, getting better by the year,” Farke said. “Physically, he’s on a top level and his pace is more than good enough I would say. He’s a very complete striker.”

He arrived at Leeds on a free transfer from Everton in August last year and when asked where he ranked among his best signings, Farke said: “At Leeds, while I’ve been here, we’ve made many top signings on a low budget.

“When I think about Joe Rodon, Ethan Ampadu, Ao Tanaka … It’s difficult to compare because as a striker you have a different role. But he’s definitely one of our better pieces of business. If you come as a free agent it doesn’t mean it costs no money because there’s a salary. But we believed in him when perhaps not many were doing this. He also believes in himself and he believes in Leeds United, so I would say he was a perfect fit.” Press Association

items.titleZh: 英超新闻：卡里克淡化对未来的疑问，阿尔特塔赞赏道曼“非凡”的发挥
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳主帅阿尔特塔对小将道曼从学生到一线队的非凡过渡表示赞赏，并支持其本赛季产生更大影响。
bodyZh: 迈克尔·卡里克表示，作为曼联主帅，他需要经历多场失利才会受到内部压力。
在老特拉福德以2比0领先的情况下，曼联周三在联赛杯中以2比3输给布莱顿。此前，他们在周日主场0比1不敌少打一人的曼城。曼联还在赛季开局客场0比2不敌赫尔城，并在本月初对阵埃弗顿的比赛中被对手在尾声阶段绝平。这些结果让卡里克受到了严格审视，在周日客场对阵富勒姆之前，人们提醒他，他的前任埃里克·滕哈赫和鲁本·阿莫林分别在任职30个月和14个月后被解雇。
当被问及何时可能面临来自曼联高层的压力时，卡里克表示：“这需要比一两场比赛的结果长得多。这对我来说并不重要。我了解这家俱乐部，了解这个角色，也知道这里对达到一定水准的要求。”
“至于未来、所有权以及我还有多长时间，这完全不存在，在我目前的位置上有这种想法是荒谬的；这根本不在考虑范围内。这是两三场比赛我们没有取得某些结果。我们必须拿出表现，我们有很多比赛要规划。”
卡里克愿意为球队的表现承担责任。“这就是我在这里的原因。这是我的责任，我对此没有异议，”他说。“这不是一场互相指责的游戏。我们总是在寻找事情来审视并寻找责任所在，有时这太过分了。责怪我吧，没问题，但这与责怪别人无关。这是关于寻找解决方案。这是一个集体的事。我知道我们想去哪里，我们想快点到那里。我们不喜欢输球，但这不会影响我们接下来要做什么。”
这位45岁的教练被问及他是否需要在场边表现出更多情绪。“我需要表现出更多情绪？以什么方式？”他回答说，“你想让我表现出什么？”
周五，JJ·加布里埃尔前往巴塞罗那，就潜在加盟该俱乐部进行商谈，据了解曼联是通过媒体才得知这一消息的，尽管这名15岁的球员已在他们那里注册。
周二，加布里埃尔告诉曼联，他希望注销注册，因为他希望加盟另一家俱乐部。皇家马德里表现出浓厚兴趣，据了解加布里埃尔及其顾问已前往巴塞罗那进行初步会谈。
卡里克说：“这种情况会自行解决，无论它将以何种方式解决。确保他一切正常是最重要的事情。” 杰米·杰克逊
米克尔·阿尔特塔称赞了马克斯·道曼从学生到阿森纳一线队成员的“非凡”过渡，并支持这名青少年本赛季产生更大影响。

在周二阿森纳在联赛杯击败伊普斯维奇的比赛中，道曼自去年崭露头角以来梅开二度，成为自2002年10月韦恩·鲁尼以来首位为英超俱乐部单场打进两球的16岁球员。这是他本赛季的首次出场，在此前阿森纳取得七连胜的比赛中，他曾四次未出场替补。道曼自14岁起就一直在阿森纳一线队随队训练，他在夏天完成了GCSE考试，在决定不参加A-Level考试后，他将攻读BTEC资格证书。阿尔特塔表示，在平衡了几年学业后，阿森纳仍在精心管理道曼的发展。
“这并不容易，”阿森纳主教练说。“这就是告诉你他所处的年龄有多疯狂，以及他在一周内需要面对的需求和竞争的生活环境。但他处理这一切的方式，包括他本人和他的家人，都是非凡的。如果他来到这里，他必须在所有条件下都在这里，我们不能在许多方面区别对待他。”
道曼有望进入周六对阵布莱顿的替补席，阿森纳正试图自1903-04赛季以伍尔维奇阿森纳身份升级以来，首次在赛季开局取得八连胜。阿尔特塔坚信，更多机会会早晚到来。“敲门的最好方式是在球场上做到，而不是在办公室里，”他说。“马克斯前几天和其他没有踢那么多时间的球员一起做的事情，真的让人印象深刻。”
英超联赛规定不允许17岁以下的球员外租，但据了解卢顿对道曼表现出了兴趣，道曼在效力阿森纳U18时曾接受过他们现任主教练杰克·威尔希尔的指导。阿尔特塔表示，道曼可能会在一月份被允许离开，届时他将年满17岁，但他目前的未来仍在阿森纳。
阿尔特塔说：“我们没有真正听取任何可能性，因为我们非常清楚，我们希望将他留在阵容中，我们希望他成为季前赛的一部分，然后从那里开始看看我们的处境。”
“我们将每六个月评估一次，我们身处何地，对他来说最好的事情是什么，然后做出正确的决定。这取决于很多因素——他需要什么，球队也需要什么，我们在阵容中拥有的人员可用性，他正在踢的分钟数以及这些分钟的质量。我们必须保持开放，但现在的重点是留在这里并对球队产生影响。” 爱德华·阿隆斯
罗伯托·德泽尔比坚称，尽管在托特纳姆热刺的开局表现喜忧参半，但桑德罗·托纳利并没有感受到身价带来的压力。这位中场球员在夏天以9250万英镑从纽卡斯尔加盟时，成为了俱乐部历史上身价最高的球员。
在曼城和阿森纳的兴趣中，德泽尔比为签下托纳利做出了巨大努力，向这位同胞发表了两个小时的推销演讲，说服他搬到北伦敦。他概述了托纳利在他的计划中将处于多么核心的地位，并解释了他可以从热刺球迷和球队足球风格中期待什么。
托纳利本赛季首发出战了全部四场英超联赛——热刺取得了两平两负且一球未进的战绩——但他的防守数据表现平平，仅创造了三次机会。
德泽尔比透露，他曾与这位26岁的球员谈过身价的重量，并声称这名球员“对此没有感到压力”。热刺主帅指出，托纳利在2020年加盟米兰的第一个赛季也花了一段时间适应，一旦在那里安顿下来，他就成为了世界上最受追捧的年轻中场之一。
德泽尔比表示，托纳利在热刺“适应得不是很快”，“但这是会发生的”，并补充道：“对于球员来说，换城市、改变一切并不是那么容易。有时适应是即时的，有时你需要更多时间。”
由于托纳利无法为前锋创造机会，热刺在门前的挣扎并未得到缓解。主场对阵埃弗顿的互交白卷是托特纳姆热刺球场140场比赛中的第一场，此前他们还在客场0比0战平诺丁汉森林，这追平了热刺在过去181场比赛中的零进球场次纪录。他们上一次在联赛中连续三场或更多场比赛互交白卷还要追溯到25岁前的乔治·格雷厄姆执教时期，当时他们连续四场没有进球。
这是一段引人注目的连胜，尤其是在夏天花费超过3亿英镑之后，这使得热刺在周六对阵阿斯顿维拉的比赛前排在第17位，维拉在经历了夏季的大变动后同样表现挣扎。
德泽尔比坚称他对托纳利表现感到满意——尽管他相信他们可以做得更好——并将其描述为“一名全能中场”。“他的身体特点是踢B2B（全能中场），但他以组织核心开始职业生涯。他在有球时足够好，在无球时也足够好。”萨姆·坎宁安
丹尼尔·法尔克在状态正佳的前锋多米尼克·卡尔沃特-勒温入选托马斯·图赫尔的英格兰代表队后，称赞他“就像一瓶好酒”。这位29岁的球员在本赛季各项赛事出场6次打进4球后，入选了三狮军团的欧国联大名单。
在周一晚埃兰路球场4比1战胜纽卡斯尔的比赛尾声被换下时，卡尔沃特-勒温受到了利兹联球迷起立鼓掌的礼遇。“多米尼克就像一瓶好酒，随着年岁增长而变得更好，”法尔克说。“在身体上，他处于顶级水平，我要说他的速度也足够好。他是一个非常全面的前锋。”
他在去年8月以自由转会的方式从埃弗顿加盟利兹联，当被问及他在自己最好的引援中排在什么位置时，法尔克说：“在利兹联，自我来到这里以来，我们在低预算下完成了许多顶级引援。”
“当我想到乔·罗登、伊桑·阿帕杜、田中碧……这很难比较，因为作为前锋，你扮演着不同的角色。但他绝对是我们最好的几笔交易之一。如果你以自由球员身份加盟，并不意味着不花钱，因为还有薪水。但当或许没有多少人这样做时，我们信任了他。他也相信自己，相信利兹联，所以我想说他是完美契合。”新闻协会

bodyEn: The poet Jorge Luis Borges wrote a famous short story about a society that had become so good at making maps, so obsessed with capturing every detail, that its rulers decided the only way to do the job right was to make a lifesize map of its entire empire, which could then be laid out across the actual land from coast to coast. Imagine a map of Britain the exact same size as Britain, showing every branch of Greggs, every nail bar, every vape shop in perfect detail. Only then can we really see what Britain looks like, by standing on a fake Britain laid over the top of actual Britain.

Borges was writing in the 1940s, at a time when people were fascinated by the mechanised future, with its new forms of measuring out the world: the wireless, the 30mph motorcar, the rise of Big Tape Measure. And to be fair, the mega-map is a pretty accurate vision of our own fully networked present, a place where you can snoop around a village in Mozambique from your laptop in Egham, where no one ever stops committing acts of minute self-surveillance, even if they think they’re just searching “What is beetroot?” on the internet.

Borges also hated football. “Soccer is popular because stupidity is popular,” he wrote, which probably seemed a bold statement at the time. But then Borges also didn’t live to see an episode of Wow Sports Premier League Breakfast at Breakfast with Roger McRoger and a puzzled Lee Trundle. After which, perhaps less of a surprise. But the process he describes is also a good description of what football is doing to itself. Endless data, endless analysis, no spaces or free air, matches that are just schematised movement. At times it can feel like football is out there laying a lifesize real-time map on top of itself.

In Borges’s story, the land soon begins to decay beneath the massive map – which is reassessed by later generations as insane, pointless and stupid – and left to rot in the desert. We haven’t reached this point. Nobody is de-mapping football. But it does perhaps explain why everyone gets so excited when a talent emerges that seems to be playful and human, to exist outside the grid. And also why it has felt wrong to gush too soon about Max Dowman, to fear placing the hex on him. We know how this works. Here is a fluffy new thing. Let us break him. Let us heap pressure on his shoulders. Don’t talk about Max Dowman. Let Max Dowman exist, breathe, bloom in the shadows.

So, Max Dowman then. It has become quite hard to ignore him. He was brilliant against Ipswich in midweek, and brilliant in a way that seems solid and real and comfortable with itself. Most obviously there were the two goals, both a perfect snapshot of why Dowman seems equipped to survive, more state‑of‑the‑art than some other young players we’ve burdened with expectation.

The second goal is particularly good, five perfect little actions packed into six seconds of football. Arsenal have the ball on the edge of the Ipswich box. Dowman shows for a pass, sees it’s going elsewhere, changes his mind, and makes a three-yard sprint to create space. Finally he has the physical capacity to control a bouncing ball in that sliver of space, to move his feet so much quicker than the nearest defender it looks like a glitch in the machine, and to finish in a way that involves sifting the options and timing the shot, all without breaking stride.

The first goal is on his other side, and involves a more classical piece of one-on-one deception. This is the same defender: Cédric Kipré, 29 years old, came through Paris Saint-Germain’s youth system. Dowman walks through him with a micro-feint and a switch of feet, then reels off another hilariously understated finish, doing it all while a second defender is still gathering himself to lunge, like a man operating in a different time signature to everyone around him.

This is the key point of difference, the ability to make everything stop, the fly-vision that means he sees what’s about to happen while everyone else is whirling about trying to read the charts, in the same way Lionel Messi (yes, sorry, sorry) always seems to have time to pass the ball into the net, like this is all a kickabout in a pair of sliders.

Our way of understanding young creative players has often seemed to lag behind where the game actually is, to be driven by nostalgia for what this thing used to look like. I remember the excitement over the 18-year-old Jack Rodwell’s physicality at the exact moment physicality was no longer going to be a thing, like proudly unveiling the latest horse‑drawn train just as the Ford Model T rolls off the production line.

Michael Owen was brilliant at 17, but he was mainly brilliant at running very fast in a straight line and smashing the ball into the net. Plus of course there was Wayne Rooney, who emerged a pale, unformed teenager composed entirely from energy drinks and white bread, out there making the game up on the fly, as though some urban foundling had come barrelling over the advert boards with a string of sausages still dangling from his mouth.

The narrative around Rooney is that he lost this vital native quality. But Rooney adapted and survived, and clearly understood what he had to be a lot better than those of us watching. And even now creative players have to exist against this. Cole Palmer is exciting because he does surprising things that seem to be striking a blow for freedom, beauty and older people who struggle to make their email work. But his real challenge is to retain just enough of this while fitting the world around him.

Dowman is a bit different. The things that make him stand out seem to speak very easily to how football is now. Being a modern creative footballer is not jinking runs, rasping drives or dribbling across a cabbage field in a pair of cowboy boots. It’s targeted energy, high-intensity semi-freedom. Lamine Yamal and Désiré Doué have the same fast-twitch foot and brain speed, the ability to operate in micro-moments, to see patterns just ahead of time. Dowman is 6ft tall and getting stronger. He won’t be kicked to pieces. He can repeat this without taking bites out of himself.

There is still the issue of his youth. But maybe this doesn’t matter so much either. The world has changed. In the age of Rooney and Owen there was no care, no data, no softness. This is where the structures of modern football are an advantage. Dowman will be GPS’d to the last decimal point. Endless physical scientists will have a say on his output and stress levels.

The money is too big. The talent is too valuable. It also comes ready to plug and play. You don’t get to this level unless you can ingest systems and briefings. You’ve already been pressure-cooked and stress-tested. What you’re being asked to do in the orderly spaces of professional football is the same thing you were asked to do in the orderly spaces of academy football, just five levels up and with more people watching.

Borges was anti-football because he saw it as inauthentic, the players no longer sports people but “actors in jerseys before the TV cameras”. And this is also fine, further evidence that boomer-dad nostalgia is one of the key archetypes of human behaviour.

Life is also different now; not harder or easier, but more instant, a series of moments, the creation of rapid-fire energy. Dowman has grown up inside this. He can parcel his time out, disappear for a bit, maybe make a show of things in the spring.

And yes, this is another way of fitting him to a model, laying a lifesize map of future Max Dowman across the present. But I strongly suspect he will be fine, and that unlike so many other things out there he’s pretty well adapted to whatever the future is supposed to look like.
items.author: Barney Ronay
items.titleZh: 我们本想让马克斯·道曼在阴影中绽放，但他如今已让人难以忽视
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳小将马克斯·道曼表现出色，展现出适应现代足球的巨大潜力。
bodyZh: 诗人豪尔赫·路易斯·博尔赫斯曾写过一篇著名的短篇小说，讲述了一个极其擅长绘制地图、痴迷于捕捉每一个细节的社会，其统治者认为把工作做好的唯一方法就是绘制一张与整个帝国等大的地图，然后将其铺在从海岸到海岸的实际土地上。想象一下一张与英国大小完全相同的英国地图，以完美的细节显示了格雷格斯的每一家分店、每一家美甲店、每一家电子烟店。只有这样，通过站在覆盖在真实英国之上的虚假英国上，我们才能真正看到英国是什么样子的。
博尔赫斯写作于20世纪40年代，当时人们对机械化的未来及其衡量世界的新方式着迷：无线电设备、时速30英里的汽车、巨型卷尺的兴起。平心而论，超级地图确实是我们现在这个完全联网的时代的精准愿景，在这里你可以通过英厄姆的笔记本电脑窥探莫桑比克的一个村庄，在这里没有人会停止进行微观的自我监视，即使他们认为自己只是在互联网上搜索“什么是甜菜根”。

博尔赫斯也讨厌足球。“足球受欢迎是因为愚蠢受欢迎，”他写道，这在当时可能是一个很大胆的说法。但博尔赫斯也没有活到看到罗杰·麦克罗杰和困惑的李·特伦德主持的《疯狂体育英超早餐》节目的那一刻。在那之后，也许就不会那么令人惊讶了。但他所描述的过程也是足球对其自身所做事情的生动写照。无休止的数据、无休止的分析、没有空间或自由空气、比赛只是图解式的运动。有时人们会觉得足球正在把一张与现实等时的地图铺在自己身上。

在博尔赫斯的故事中，巨大的地图之下的土地很快就开始腐烂——后来几代人重新评估其为疯狂、毫无意义和愚蠢——并任其在沙漠中腐烂。我们还没有到达这一点。没有人会取消足球的地图化。但这也许可以解释为什么当一个看起来俏皮、有人情味且存在于网格之外的天才涌现时，每个人都会如此兴奋。这也解释了为什么过早对马克斯·道曼大加赞赏会让人感觉不对劲，并担心给他带来魔咒。我们知道这是怎么回事。这是一个毛茸茸的新东西。让我们摧毁他。让我们把压力压在他的肩膀上。不要谈论马克斯·道曼。让马克斯·道曼存在、呼吸并在阴影中绽放。
那么，说说马克斯·道曼吧。现在要忽视他变得相当困难。他在周中的比赛中对阵伊普斯威奇时表现出色，这种出色显得扎实、真实且内心笃定。最明显的是那两个进球，这两个进球都是完美的快照，解释了为什么道曼似乎具备生存的能力，比我们赋予期望的其他一些年轻球员更具现代感。
第二个进球格外精彩，在六秒钟的足球比赛中包含了五个完美的微小动作。阿森纳在伊普斯威奇禁区边缘控球。道曼寻求传球，发现球传向别处，改变了主意，并进行了三码的冲刺来创造空间。最终，他在那个狭小的空间里具备了控制弹地球的身体能力，其挪动双脚的速度比最近的防守球员快得多，看起来就像机器出了故障，并且能够通过筛选选项和掌握射门时机的方式完成破门，而且全程步伐没有丝毫停顿。
第一个进球在她的另一侧，涉及更经典的一对一欺骗。这是同一名防守球员：塞德里克·基普雷，29岁，出自巴黎圣日耳曼青训营。道曼通过一次微假动作和脚法切换轻松过掉了他，随后又完成了一次令人捧腹的低调射门，这一切发生时，第二名防守球员还在调整身体准备扑抢，就像一个在与周围所有人处于不同时空节奏中运作的人。
这是关键的区别所在，这种让一切都停下来的能力，这种飞行般的视野意味着当其他所有人都在疯狂旋转试图解读图表时，他能看到即将发生的事情，就像莱昂内尔·梅西（是的，对不起，对不起）总是似乎有时间把球传进球门一样，就好像这一切只是穿着拖鞋在踢野球一样。
我们理解年轻创造型球员的方式似乎总是滞后于比赛的实际现状，并受到对过去事物怀旧情绪的驱使。我记得当18岁的杰克·罗德威尔的身体素质在身体素质不再重要的那一刻引发轰动时，就像在福特T型车刚下生产线时自豪地展示最新的马车火车一样。
迈克尔·欧文在17岁时就非常出色，但他主要的出色之处在于直线跑得非常快并将球轰入球网。当然还有韦恩·鲁尼，他作为一个面色苍白、尚未成型的青少年出现，完全由能量饮料和白面包组成，在场上即兴发挥，就像某种城市弃儿嘴里还叼着一串香肠越过广告牌狂奔而来一样。
围绕鲁尼的叙事是他失去了这种至关重要的本土特质。但鲁尼适应并生存了下来，并且显然比我们这些旁观者更清楚他必须成为什么样的人。即使在现在，创造型球员也必须在这种环境下生存。科尔·帕尔默令人兴奋，因为他做出了令人惊讶的事情，似乎在为自由、美以及那些电子邮件运行困难的老年人进行抗争。但他真正的挑战是在适应周围世界的同时，保留足够多的这种特质。
道曼则有些不同。让他脱颖而出的特质似乎非常契合现代足球的发展方向。现代创造型足球运动员不是花哨的盘带、刺耳的抽射，也不是穿着牛仔靴在菜地里盘带。而是有针对性的能量、高强度的半自由。亚马尔和杜埃拥有相同的快速应变脚法和头脑速度，具备在微观时刻运作的能力，能够在稍早前看到比赛的规律。道曼身高六英尺，而且身体变得更强壮了。他不会被踢得支离破碎。他可以重复这一点而不会消耗自己。
年轻仍然是个问题。但也许这也不是那么重要。世界已经变了。在鲁尼和欧文的时代，没有关怀，没有数据，没有温情。这就是现代足球结构发挥优势的地方。道曼将被精确到小数点后最后一位的GPS定位。无休止的体能科学家将对他的输出和压力水平发表意见。
资金太庞大了。天赋太宝贵了。它也做好了即插即用的准备。你若不具备吸收战术体系和简报的能力，就无法达到这个水平。你已经被高压烹调和压力测试过了。在职业足球有序的空间里被要求做的事情，和你在学院足球有序的空间里被要求做的事情是一样的，只是级别更高，有更多的人在观看。
博尔赫斯反足球是因为他认为足球是不真实的，球员不再是运动员，而是“电视摄像机前的球衣演员”。这也是可以理解的，这进一步证明了嬉皮士老爸式的怀旧是人类行为的关键原型之一。
生活现在也不同了；不是更难或更容易，而是更加瞬息万变，是一系列瞬间，是快速爆发能量的创造。道曼就是在这种环境下长大的。他可以分配自己的时间，消失一会儿，也许在春天大显身手。
是的，这也是将他纳入某种模版、将未来马克斯·道曼的等大地图铺在现实之上的另一种方式。但我坚信他会没事的，与外界许多其他事物不同，他非常适应未来的模样。

bodyEn: Chelsea have not won this west London derby since Brentford’s first Premier League season. Each visit since October 2021’s 1-0 win, Ben Chilwell the scorer, has been a draw. This season has continued the divergence between the clubs’ respective approaches, Brentford’s solidity and continuity contrasting with Chelsea attempting their latest reboot. Kevin Schade, after two well-taken goals at Bournemouth, will fancy facing a defence not yet attuned to Xabi Alonso’s configurations. Only one team has won a Premier League title with a defensive trio: Chelsea’s last title team, in 2016-17 under Antonio Conte. Alonso’s attack has been rather more successful, presenting another challenge for Jannik Schuster. Replacing Nathan Collins, the 20-year-old central defender had a tough examination from Bournemouth’s Evanilson on his first Premier League start, emerging with credit. For Chelsea, João Pedro has three goals and three assists, but doubts surrounding his fitness could lead to Danny Welbeck’s first league start. John Brewin
Brentford v Chelsea, Friday 8pm (all times BST)

What happens when a very stoppable force meets an extremely movable object? We will be tuning into events at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday to find out as 19th-placed Aston Villa arrive in north London. The teams have scored one goal between them in the league and are desperately hoping for a first Premier League win. The return of Pedro Porro is big for Roberto De Zerbi and that should bring the Archie Gray Experiment at right-back to a merciful end. No Premier League starting XI feels less settled than Spurs – most players look as if they are a mistake or two from being dropped – which has culminated in a side that seems governed by fear and continuously prefers to take the safe option. After coming off the bench against Everton and Liverpool in the past week, the injury-plagued James Maddison will be itching to start and take some sort of initiative for Tottenham. Michael Butler
Tottenham v Aston Villa, Saturday 12.30pm

When Fabian Hürzeler spoke about Brighton’s success being founded on them being “well structured” after their stirring comeback against Manchester United at Old Trafford on Wednesday, he could have been referring to Malick Yalcouyé. The 20-year-old Ivorian moved to the south coast in 2024 after spending just a few months with IFK Gothenburg in Sweden but had to wait until this season to make his senior debut for Brighton after being sent on loan to Sturm Graz in Austria and then Swansea last season. With Jack Hinshelwood sidelined by injury until after the international break, Yalcouyé has taken his chance in the No 10 role and already found the net twice in the Premier League as Brighton have made a brilliant start. Arsenal are up next for the division’s top scorers – who have 13 goals from their opening four matches – and Mikel Arteta should be wary of the threat posed by Yalcouyé and co as the champions prepare for a fourth away game in succession. Ed Aarons
Brighton v Arsenal, Saturday 3pm

Vitalii Mykolenko’s early-season improvement has gone largely unheralded – and it probably always will be among his detractors – but at a time when David Moyes needs experienced players to step up and defy the constraints of a small squad, the Everton left-back has produced. Having signed a new three-year contract in the summer, and seemingly bulked up, the Ukraine international has kept his critics quiet with several impressive displays for a defence that has four clean sheets in six matches. There remains a problematic lack of cover at left-back after the decision to loan Adam Aznou to Málaga for the season but Mykolenko, the better defender, has eased the concerns that surrounded his position before the new campaign. Ipswich’s new forward recruits, Emersonn and Zian Flemming, will test Everton’s solidity but Moyes’s side will have made an encouraging start should they sign off with a win before the extended international break. Andy Hunter
Everton v Ipswich, Saturday 3pm

As befits a lover of direct football, Matthias Jaissle likes to get straight to the point. On Thursday he was asked whether, in the light of Monday night’s 4-1 thrashing at Leeds and a raft of injuries, he was tempted to perhaps switch to a back five or modify his beloved “vertical” approach when Hull visit Tyneside on Saturday. The reply proved unequivocal. “No,” said a manager unafraid to answer questions with a single word. Instead Jaissle expects his young team to retain faith in a wider vision as Newcastle – who signed eight players aged 24 and under this summer – adapt to life after Bruno Guimarães, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon. “It’s a brave journey the club is going on and I’m fully committed in that,” the German said. “If there’s one setback, we shouldn’t delete our journey or our vision. We’re fully committed. We’re fully aligned. We anticipated that something like that against Leeds would happen. It’s on us to respond. But while still believing. We don’t change.” Louise Taylor
Newcastle v Hull, Saturday 3pm

Many scoffed at the £45m that was paid for Liam Delap in the summer but Nottingham Forest feels like the perfect place for the striker to regain his form. Forest previously thrived with the now injured Chris Wood as their arrowhead and Delap is something of a younger regent for the New Zealander – powerful, instinctive and willing to bring others into play. During Saturday’s win at Villa, Morgan Gibbs-White and Delap looked as if they already have an understanding and both will be keen to capitalise against a Coventry side that have conceded eight goals in the past two games. After a nervy campaign last season, Forest feel back in the ascendancy and will have been delighted that plans to increase the City Ground’s capacity from 31,000 to 52,500, at an estimated cost of £790m, were approved by the local council on Wednesday. MB
Nottingham Forest v Coventry, Saturday 5.30pm

After watching Bournemouth make their European bow from afar in San Sebastián, a city Andoni Iraola knows inside out, the Basque head coach will return to his previous club on Sunday. Iraola – whose assistants Tommy Elphick and Shaun Cooper played for Bournemouth, the former captaining the club into the Premier League in 2015 – led the Dorset club into the Europa League by recording their best-ever finish, sixth. His body of work on the south coast earned him the Liverpool opportunity and a warm welcome is a guarantee. Despite the Cherries’ slow start under Iraola’s successor, Marco Rose, they will pose tricky opposition. items.titleEn: Arsenal reach 500 Premier League clean sheets
items.summaryEn: Our shutout against Burnley on Monday night saw us hit the milestone - here are all the stats behind that massive total
bodyEn: A fourth league victory in a row was claimed against Burnley on Monday night, with another rock-solid defensive performance ultimately paving the way towards a massive three points.

We've kept clean sheets in all four of those recent wins to put us within touching distance of the Premier League title, and the latest blank against the Clarets brought up a significant milestone, as it was our 500th in the competition.

Since our formation in 1992, only two other teams have recorded more shoutouts than we have, and we have been chasing down both Manchester United and Chelsea at the top of the leaderboard in recent seasons.
Most clean sheets in Premier League history
Another 19 have been added to our tally in 2025/26, and only in 1998/99 and 1993/94 (when we played 42 games) have we recorded more in a single Premier League season.

David Raya’s displays in goal have been crucial to our defensive stability, and the now three-time Golden Glove winner has been responsible for nearly 10% of our overall tally, despite patrolling our posts for just three seasons.

Twice this season, we have gone four Premier League games without conceding, while no other team has managed more three. Our best run in the Premier League is eight in a row, which we strung together during our 1997/98 title triumph, when the late Alex Manninger contributed six of them.

The other two came from David Seaman, and unexpectedly, given his lengthy ownership of our number one jersey, he is way out in front as the Gunners goalie who has kept the most clean sheets, while Jens Lehmann is only other keeper now in front of our current custodian:
Arsenal goalkeepers with most PL clean sheets
But he would be quick to share the acclaim with his backline, and some members of a very familiar back four appear highly on our list of defenders who have also contributed to our 500 clean sheets:
Arsenal defenders with most PL clean sheets
As for opponents, Newcastle United have found it hard to find a way past us most often, with us keeping 32 clean sheets in 62 matches, while 28 in 60 have been registered against West Ham United:
Opponents we've kept most PL clean sheets against

As for anyone wanting a good omen ahead of the final game of the season against Crystal Palace, we have 12 clean sheets in 33 Premier League games against the Eagles, including four of the last seven meetings, with Raya donning the gloves for three of those. One more this weekend could go a long way to getting his mitts on the trophy he really craves for the first time.

items.titleEn: Trio nominated for PL Player of the Season
items.summaryEn: Gabriel, David Raya and Declan Rice have been named on an eight-player shortlist
bodyEn: A trio of Gunners have been nominated for the Premier League Player of the Season award, and your votes can help one of them win the prestigious award.

Gabriel, David Raya and Declan Rice have been named on an eight-player shortlist of those who have shone brightest in the division during 2025/26, with our stars helping us to the brink of the league title with two games still to play.

Big Gabi is nominated after another standout season in the heart of our defence. He has contributed at both ends of the pitch, scoring three goals and assisting four more, while also helping us to a competition-low 26 goals conceded so far, thanks to an incredible 88.2% successful pass rate, winning two-thirds of his duels, and making 34 blocks and 23 interceptions.

David has already secured the Premier League Golden Glove for the third successive season, having registered 18 clean sheets in 36 matches. He has made a string of impressive and incredible saves stretching back to matchday one when he somehow denied Manchester United’s Mathes Cunha, one of a number of nominations for Save of the Month, which he won in December for an incredible stop to deny Brighton & Hove Albion's Yankuba Minteh.

Declan meanwhile has been the heartbeat of our midfield, missing only one league game during the campaign. His versatility has seen him operate in front of our back four or behind our frontline, while his threat from set-pieces has been a key component of our title push and has seen him register five league assists, while also contributing with four goals of his own, including a brace in a key win against Bournemouth in January.

The five other contenders include the top two scorers in the division, Manchester City’s Erling Haaland and Brentford’s breakout star, Igor Thiago, while Manchester United playmaker Bruno Fernandes is recognised for assisting 19 times so far.

Morgan Gibbs-White's impressive haul of 13 league goals gets him a place on the shortlist, where the Nottingham Forest man is joined by Antoine Semenyo, who has impressed for both Bournemouth and Manchester City either side of January.

The award, which has been presented since 1995, has previously been won by three Gunners. Patrick Vieira was the first in 2000/01, with Freddie Ljungberg claiming it the year after. Thierry Henry was then awarded it twice in 2003/04 and 2005/06, meaning we could end a 20-year wait to see one of our players join the illustrious roll of honour, with Liverpool’s Mohamed Salah the current holder.
Supporters' votes will be added to the opinions of a panel of experts to determine the winner, so make sure you cast your ballot before 12pm on Monday, May 18.

items.titleEn: Norgaard takes on AMA challenge on Reddit!
items.summaryEn: Check out what Christian Norgaard had to say in our latest 'ask me anything' Reddit challenge
bodyEn: Danish midfielder Christian Norgaard has become our latest star to take on questions from our Reddit channel as part of our Ask Me Anything series!
Following on from William Saliba, our number 16 was in the hotseat, answering questions from being a father, to the funniest player in the team and much more!
First up, Christian was asked about his work-life balance at Arsenal compared to previous sides he's played for.

He said: "I think it's very hard to find that right work-life balance when you're in such a competitive environment where it is about winning and it's not only about winning, it's about trying to achieve bigger things than just winning in the weekend.
"So it takes a lot and it takes a tone as well on the private part, but I have a really understanding wife and some fantastic kids that are supporting me throughout."
Next up, the Dane was asked about making his Champions League debut this season with us.

He said: "The first Champions League game was special. First of all, coming on against Bilbao, only if it was just for a couple of minutes, was a fantastic feeling. But my first start in Prague against Slavia was something else.

"I think when you're standing on the pitch and you hear the anthem, it gives you a special feeling. So I've been very fortunate to play quite a lot in the Champions League and I've enjoyed every game."
We saw some special moments during Christian's signing video as he was greeted by his son the big day.

Asked about what fatherhood has taught him, he said: "Humility, I think. That's something I try and teach my boys every day, to say thank you and be polite. You'll come far in life just by being humble.
"It doesn't matter if you're good or bad at different stuff, but your personality, how you approach interactions with others, is important for me."
To see the rest of Christian's answers, head to our official Reddit channel. You can also watch the best moments by pressing play on the video above!

items.titleEn: Carabao Cup final: Useful information for our fans
items.summaryEn: Find out about travel news, fan zones, stadium access, bag policies and more before heading to Wembley
bodyEn: Ahead of Sunday’s Carabao Cup final against Manchester City, here is some information to help all our supporters plan their day at Wembley Stadium as we go searching for our first piece of silverware of 2025/26:
TRAVEL
There are no known disruptions on any Tube or London Overground services. Please aim to arrive at the stadium early and check Transport for London’s updates for the latest news and information.
Event day parking at Wembley Stadium is limited and must be booked in advance via Wembley Official Parking.
FAN ZONES
If you're heading to Wembley, join us for the ultimate pre-match build-up at our dedicated fanzone in BOXPARK Wembley.
Doors open from 9am, with tickets guaranteeing entry if you arrive before 12:30pm. Tickets are available online now, and will be available on the day on a first-come, first-served basis.

Getting you in the mood for the game, there will be DJ sets, our matchday brass band, a Gunnersaurus appearance, and matchday host Nigel Mitchell running segments throughout the afternoon, including a match preview and legends interviews, with Lee Dixon already confirmed and more names to follow.
Entry is exclusive to Arsenal supporters and a valid match ticket is required. Alcohol will be served until 3.30pm, before the venue closes at 4pm.
PUBLIC SPACE PROTECTION ORDER

No drinking of alcohol is permitted on Olympic Way and the surrounding area for all events at Wembley Stadium, and supporters drinking alcohol in these areas ahead of the final will be asked to hand over their alcohol and enforcement action may be considered.
Supporters wanting alcohol before the game should head to the designated Arsenal pubs in the area east of Wembley Stadium.
STADIUM ACCESS
Doors open at 1.30pm for hospitality guests, while general admission is from 2.30pm. Our supporters will be housed on the east side of the stadium, which can be accessed to the left of Wembley Way.

Please refer to your ticket for your turnstile colour zone. The quickest route to your turnstile entry point is by following the signage for the colour zone. Please ensure you enter via the correct turnstile.
Please make sure you arrive at the stadium in good time to assist with security protocols. We advise all supporters to enter the stadium early to avoid queues.
Guests under the age of 14 must be accompanied by an adult. Children under the age of two are not permitted into the stadium.
BAG POLICY

Wembley Stadium operates a restricted bag policy. Each person can only bring one small bag into the stadium, and it must not be bigger than A4 size (H297mm/11.7 inches, W210mm/8.27 inches, D210mm/8.27 inches).

Please note, this means the overall bag size - bags that are half-full and folded over to reduce their size will not be accepted. Anyone carrying bags that do not meet the criteria above will not be allowed into the stadium.
A bag drop facility is available outside the Ibis Hotel. Please note there is a charge for this service.
LICENCED STANDING

Wembley Stadium has installed 5,000 licensed standing seats on both sides of level 5 for the 2026 season. Only those with licensed standing printed on their tickets are allowed to stand in this section. Standing is permitted throughout these areas.
EMIRATES STADIUM TOUR

Cup final day doesn't have to begin at Wembley - it can start in N5 too! On the morning of the final, Emirates Stadium Tour doors open early, giving every Gooner the perfect excuse to make a proper morning of it before kick-off.
There's no better warm-up than a Stadium Tour, a browse through The Armoury to pick up your kit, then take a walk through our Museum, and leave feeling ready that more history will be created.
Opening hours:Armoury: 9am to 3pmStadium Tour & Museum: 9am to 3pm (last entry 2pm)
Book now
MORE INFORMATION
A full guide to everything else you may need to know about the final can be found on Wembley Stadium's Carabao Cup final supporters guide.

items.titleEn: An open letter from Renée Slegers
items.summaryEn: Renée Slegers pens an open letter to our supporters after signing a new contract as Arsenal Women head coach
bodyEn: Dear Arsenal,

Our story started a long time ago. I was a young footballer, 17 years old and sharing a pitch with heroes I’d seen lift the Champions League trophy for the first time. Kelly Smith, Alex Scott, Karen Carney, Rachel Yankey, Anita Asante, Faye White, Jayne Ludlow…these are legendary names that meant so much back then and mean even more now.
The club gave me something: perspective, gratitude, inspiration. My dreams came alive.
Arsenal still gives me that.

To me, football has always been about people, life, and seeing it come together on the grass. How players combine, how they move, how the ball moves – it’s beautiful. The game is growing so fast, but I want to stay close to its essence: connection.

Moving forward as a collective is what drives me. Young players breaking through, working together with experienced players and staff, some who have been moving the game forward long before I joined the club. Our goal is to honour the work of people before us and continue that legacy.

Sharing these moments is what makes me so proud to be at Arsenal. What we stand for off the pitch and our connection with you, the supporters, is so special. I feel gratitude every time I walk through the tunnel and see that sea of red and white.

I look at the Champions League final, that day in Lisbon when everybody – players, staff, supporters – was at their best. We were prepared, every detail was right and we knew how to tackle every scenario. That memory will stay with me forever. But I believe it was only the beginning of what we can do together.
My ambition is that we can continue to achieve our way, the Arsenal way. This is a club that’s so rich with history, but we will always be hungry for more. That makes me so excited for the future.
That future starts now.
Best wishes,Renée Slegers

items.titleEn: “We help young people address trauma”
items.summaryEn: Arsenal has helped to fund the Baobab Centre, a therapeutic community that offers support to survivors of human rights absuse
bodyEn: The Arsenal Foundation has helped to fund the Baobab Centre, a non-residential therapeutic community that offers holistic support to young survivors of human rights abuses seeking refuge in the UK. Baobab director Sheila Melzak, who is 75 and was herself a refugee from eastern Europe, tells us about their work.
“I have always been interested in the strength and dilemmas of people who have been separated from their parents, communities and culture.

“When I finished a university degree in psychology, I ran a children’s home for many years in Hackney. I trained as a child and adolescent psychotherapist and worked in CAMHS community mental health services. I went to work at an organisation that worked with torture survivors which is now called Freedom from Torture.

“I worked there for almost 20 years with young people who were separated from their parents or those living with parents who were unable to care for them for various reasons. A group of us decided to set up a new organisation that could focus on the special needs of children and adolescents who came in the UK seeking asylum after experiences of human rights abuses and who were separated from their families. We set up this new organisation and it became a charity in 2010.

“The Baobab Centre for Young Survivors in Exile has a holistic approach with a multidisciplinary team that attends to the internal emotional needs and the external practical needs of vulnerable young people seeking asylum in the UK. Once young people gain refugee status they continue to have many practical problems accessing education, work, benefits and more in a culture that is very different to the culture where they grew up.

“The Baobab Centre offers individual and group psychotherapy and various group activities, and we operate as a community because we see that much of the therapeutic involvement comes from participation in community life. For example, we run annual retreats to the countryside and organise many day activities. We also hold a monthly community meeting where young people and staff share a meal together and can discuss issues to do with life in the UK, the situation in the world including conflicts and specific issues at Baobab.

“Our aim is that young people who have experienced violence and loss and many unpleasant changes in their lives are fortified in our transitional community so that they might thrive in the community of exile and contribute to community life.

“The staff and young people find exercise to be therapeutic in that it reduces tension and anxieties within their bodies. We’ve used The Arsenal Foundation money for our Hardship Fund, and specifically towards supporting the mental wellbeing of young refugees and asylum seekers through improving their access to sports and exercise activities. The funding enabled young people to access gym memberships and enabled us to contribute to destitutions funds – many young people go through periods of destitution.

“When many young people arrive in the UK their credibility is challenged, including their age. If the people assessing them don’t believe they are minors, they are placed in Home Office accommodation and given very little money to live on. All the young people who come to the centre suffer serious mental health issues and developmental difficulties.

“They enjoy and seem to flourish having exercise. They also all love watching football. In the past we’ve had some of our supporters take our young people to Arsenal and they love having the opportunity of seeing a real football match, and we are looking forward to a trip to Emirates Stadium that has been made possible thanks to this grant.

“We hope that their future involves building a new life and recovering from trauma. It’s our experience that if our young people are able to face the difficulties in their lives as well as celebrate the opportunities they have had and have in the present they will be best able to cope with the challenges of life in the future. We aim to help the young people address the impact of trauma, separation and loss and to build a meaningful life in the UK.”
